title: TE Connectivity at OCP Summit 2026 The Interview
gist: Interview with TE Connectivity's Brian Payne at OCP Summit 2026: TE, with NVIDIA and Cisco, announced a USFP standard for 448G per-lane front-panel connectivity, is dual-investing in copper backplanes and co-packaged optics (incl. the RAM Photonics acquisition), and is pathfinding sidecar power racks, horizontal liquid-cooled busbars and 800V rack-to-rack power toward megawatt-class AI racks, backed by 10 DDN-dedicated factories.

insights.claim: TE Connectivity, in partnership with NVIDIA and Cisco, announced at the October 2026 OCP Global Summit a new front-panel module standard for 448G per-lane SerDes, shown as a 3D-printed USFP model in a QSFP-like form factor.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: An NVIDIA/Cisco-backed form factor for 448G gives TE a design-win position in next-gen AI networking pluggables; watch adoption vs competing 448G proposals.
insights.quote: in a partnership with NVIDIA and Cisco, we announced our new standard for getting to 448.

insights.claim: The industry has two competing models for reaching 448G per-lane front-panel connectivity, with thermal and signal-integrity trade-offs driving a standards contest that TE Connectivity believes its NVIDIA/Cisco-backed design will win.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A form-factor standards battle at 448G creates winners and losers among connector and transceiver suppliers; track which design hyperscalers and switch vendors adopt.
insights.quote: I would say there are two competing models out there.

insights.claim: TE Connectivity's USFP 448G design mechanically separates power delivery from the signal path to protect signal integrity, and is built to accept cold-plate liquid cooling as transceiver power rises.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Pluggable transceiver power is rising enough that front-panel optics may need liquid cooling — a tailwind for cold-plate and thermal suppliers.
insights.quote: as we see the power of the transceiver escalate, we’ll be able to do cold plate liquid cooling to pull heat out of the system.

insights.claim: Copper backplanes combined with midplanes are a key unlock for AI rack-scale systems, letting compute sleds and GPUs be separated and reconnected through a midplane, and TE Connectivity claims to be one of very few companies able to produce them in massive volumes.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: High-volume copper backplane/midplane manufacturing is a scarce capability, supporting pricing power for the few qualified suppliers in AI rack interconnect.
insights.quote: TE is one of the only companies in the industry that’s able to do that.

insights.claim: TE Connectivity positions itself as covering the full AI data path from chip to switch: near-chip packaging, optics, front and back I/O connectivity, and the cabling in between, all deployed at massive scale today.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Breadth across the interconnect stack means TE's DDN revenue scales with AI rack content per system, not just unit volumes.
insights.quote: We are focused from the chip all the way to the switch.
insights.locator: TE is one of the only companies

insights.claim: Copper remains state of the art for AI interconnect despite predictions of its demise since 10 Gigabit Ethernet, so TE Connectivity is pursuing a dual investment in both copper and optics rather than pivoting fully to optics.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Do not over-discount copper interconnect vendors on the co-packaged optics narrative; the transition is gradual and both will grow.
insights.quote: copper is still the state of the art

insights.claim: Co-packaged optics is becoming real now, unlike a decade ago, because the physics of how far copper can be routed breaks down as lane counts rise, forcing an eventual pivot to optics.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Rising lane counts per rack are the forcing function for CPO adoption; watch lane-count and reach limits at 448G as the trigger for optics share gains.
insights.quote: There is a point in time where we will have to make the pivot.
insights.locator: Folks have been talking about co-packaged optics

insights.claim: TE Connectivity acquired optics company RAM Photonics in 2026 and is massively investing in co-packaged optics and co-packaged copper as part of its optical pathfinding.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: M&A signals TE is buying into optics to hedge copper displacement; a data point for photonics-startup acquisition appetite among connector majors.
insights.quote: Earlier this year, we acquired an optics company, RAM Photonics.

insights.claim: Serviceable connectors that plug into the chip package are a new innovation enabling co-packaged optics to reach mass deployment, since serviceability at scale is a critical design vector that was unsolved five or six years ago.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Serviceability, not just signal performance, gates CPO volume ramps; suppliers solving field-replaceable CPO connectors capture value.
insights.quote: serviceability is a critical design vector that drives innovation.
insights.locator: One of the things you’re showing in the booth

themes.theme: Sidecar power racks and liquid-cooled busbars

insights.claim: AI racks lack the power density to fit chips, switches and power distribution in one rack, which is driving sidecar designs where a full adjacent rack is dedicated to power distribution and cooling.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Sidecar power racks add new rack-level content (power shelves, busbars, cooling) per AI deployment — a growth vector for power-delivery suppliers.
insights.quote: We simply don’t have the power density today to fit all of that in one rack
insights.locator: Power: The Sidecar Power Rack and Horizontal Busbar

insights.claim: TE Connectivity built a horizontal, rack-spanning busbar — which it says nobody else has done — for one of its large customers, delivering power from a sidecar power rack into the adjacent IT rack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Custom power solutions for large customers indicate hyperscaler-driven design wins in rack power distribution.
insights.quote: we’ve actually got a busbar that runs horizontally, which is unique in the industry. Nobody’s done that.

insights.claim: Busbars and solutions to power-constrained half-full racks were discussed for years but only took hold with the AI boom, which led to liquid-cooled busbars spanning racks to avoid raising current and heat dissipation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AI demand converted long-stalled data center power innovations into real deployments; liquid-cooled power distribution is now an addressable market.
insights.quote: none of that really took hold until the AI boom
insights.locator: Right. In this industry, we have talked about power constraints

insights.claim: Reaching a megawatt of power per rack will require 800V distribution, and TE Connectivity is pathfinding 800V liquid-cooled busbars and prototype rack-to-rack 800V cables.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 800V DC rack power is the next data center power transition; suppliers of HV busbars, cables and conversion gear stand to benefit.
insights.quote: pushing towards 800 volt. That’s what’s going to be necessary to get to a megawatt of power at the rack level.
insights.locator: The next frontier is high voltage.

insights.claim: Because every power conversion step incurs losses, the efficient 800V architecture aims to carry 800V from the source through busways into the rack and across it, with liquid cooling as a critical element.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Fewer conversion stages favor end-to-end HV power architectures and vendors with whip-to-chip portfolios over point-product suppliers.
insights.quote: Every conversion has losses associated with it.

insights.claim: TE Connectivity claims to be one of the few, if not the only, companies focused on the entire whip-to-chip power delivery chain of the AI rack, letting it see bottlenecks before they occur.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: System-level power plus connectivity positioning could make TE a strategic hyperscaler partner as racks approach 1MW.
insights.quote: We’re one of the few, if not the only, company focused on the entire power delivery of the AI infrastructure at the AI rack.

themes.theme: TE DDN growth and manufacturing scale

insights.claim: TE Connectivity's Digital Data Networks (DDN) business has experienced massive growth over the last three years driven by AI infrastructure buildouts.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: DDN is TE's AI-exposed segment; track its growth as a read on hyperscaler AI capex flowing to interconnect and power content.
insights.quote: We have experienced massive growth over the last three years
insights.locator: Patrick Kennedy: Could you give us a little bit of background

insights.claim: TE Connectivity operates 10 manufacturing facilities across China, Southeast Asia and North America dedicated solely to its DDN business, to mass-produce AI infrastructure parts for hyperscalers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Dedicated, geographically diversified capacity supports volume ramps and mitigates single-region supply/geopolitical risk.
insights.quote: We have 10 manufacturing facilities around the world, from China to Southeast Asia to North America, all focused just on the DDN business
insights.locator: Then that’s when we’ve got to shift to

insights.claim: Hyperscalers are building AI data centers at a breakneck pace and chip cycles have accelerated, forcing interconnect and power suppliers to iterate designs with customers well ahead of mass production.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Faster chip cadence compresses supplier design cycles, favoring suppliers with R&D depth and close hyperscaler co-design.

insights.claim: Brian Payne, a 26-year Dell veteran, joined TE Connectivity as Vice President of Product Management for the DDN business about a month before the 2026 OCP Global Summit.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Hiring a long-time Dell server product leader signals TE's push toward system-level, rack-scale product management.
